analyst_comment: November events were delivered with in-house crew and staging stock instead of the subcontracting assumed in budget; Q4 freight was also renegotiated. Genuine savings, not a timing shift. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-12-10)

An unplanned client project was won in late March and delivered inside April; external production was booked at short-notice premium rates. Together with the matching revenue line the net margin impact is slightly negative. Change-order discipline flagged to the project director. (FP&A Analyst, 2026-05-12)
Fewer freelance crew days in a light January build schedule; the permanent technical team covered the work. Volume, consistent with the month's activity. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-02-10)
A client brought part of its September roadshow forward into July. Timing between months rather than new business; the September shortfall stayed within tolerance. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-08-11)
Unbudgeted revenue from the same late-won April project; see the matching COGS variance. Recognized on delivery. (FP&A Analyst, 2026-05-12)
Production costs of the pulled-forward October activation; see the matching revenue variance. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-11-08)
A brand activation sold for early 2025 was pulled into October at the client's request. The matching cost variance appears on the COGS line the same month. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-11-08)
Contractor spend deferred during the summer staffing gap on the delivery bench; caught up from September. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-08-09)

External development spend paused over the year-end delivery freeze and resumed in February, alongside the two go-lives that slipped on the revenue line. This recurs every holiday season; budget phasing to be corrected in the next cycle. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-02-10)
Freelance day rates paused over the same summer gap as the deferred contractor work; see the matching external production variance. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-08-09)
Freelance motion designers booked to cover a vacant post through the November campaign peak. The permanent hire started in January. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-12-10)
Freelance bookings paused with the two platform go-lives that slipped into February; see the matching revenue variance. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-02-10)

Two platform go-lives slipped from January into February on client-side content delays. Revenue is recognized on delivery, so January carries the gap; both projects were invoiced in February. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-02-10)
One retainer client commissioned an out-of-cycle campaign microsite in an otherwise quiet August. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-09-09)

January carried final supplier invoices for a December 2023 conference that arrived after the prior-year cut-off. Timing across the year-end, no change to the full-year run-rate. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-02-09)
The June conference was held in a client-owned venue instead of the hired venue assumed in budget; venue and catering pass-through came in under plan. A saving, not timing. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-07-09)
Delivery costs of the two milestones that slipped into November were held back with them; see the matching revenue variance. Timing only. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-11-08)
Two May engagements ran on the in-house registration platform rather than the external provider budgeted for them; supplier spend under plan. A saving, not timing. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-06-10)

The September summit required additional security screening and accreditation staffing imposed by the host ministry after the budget was set; only part of it could be recharged. (FP&A Analyst, 2025-10-10)
Two institutional clients pushed their October milestone invoicing into November after a budget-cycle approval delay on their side. Timing only. (FP&A Analyst, 2024-11-08)
